+When the privilege mode is S, VS, or U, the following holds:

body:
The condition “When the privilege mode is S, VS, or U” is confusing for `scrdirty`: (1) `scrdirty` is an SRW CSR (so U-mode cannot access it), and (2) when running with V=1 in VS/VU, `vscrdirty` substitutes for `scrdirty`. Consider rewording this condition to reflect the relevant execution state (e.g., V=0 and privilege in {S,U}, and describe VS/VU behavior only under `vscrdirty`).
```suggestion
When V=0 and instructions execute in S or U privilege modes, the following holds for `scrdirty`:
* When ``scrdirty[__i__]`` is set to Clean, executing any instruction that changes the state of CR #__i__ will change ``scrdirty[__i__]`` to Dirty.
* Implementations may also change ``scrdirty[__i__]`` from Clean to Dirty at any time, even when there is no change in CR #__i__ state.
When V=1 and instructions execute in VS or VU modes, an analogous behavior is defined for `vscrdirty` (see <<ACE-CSR-vscrdirty>>).
```

body:
The rule “any instruction that changes the state of CR #i will change `scrdirty[i]` to Dirty” appears to conflict with the later normative statement that `ace.clear` “does not make `*status.ACES` Dirty” (since `ace.clear` unconfigures a CR and therefore changes its state). Please clarify whether unconfigure/reset operations are excluded from dirty tracking, or narrow the wording here (e.g., only instructions that modify the content of a configured CR).
```suggestion
* When ``scrdirty[__i__]`` is set to Clean, executing any instruction that modifies the content of a configured CR #__i__ (for example, writes CC metadata or content) will change ``scrdirty[__i__]`` to Dirty. Operations that only configure, unconfigure, or reset a CR without modifying its cryptographic content are excluded from this rule.
```

body: The `scrdirty` definition earlier says any instruction that changes CR state must set the corresponding dirty bit, but the `ace.clear` section here no longer specifies how `ace.clear` affects `*crdirty`/`*status.ACES`. Given `ace.clear` unconfigures CR state, the current text reads as potentially contradictory with the earlier “changes the state ⇒ set Dirty” rule. Please explicitly state `ace.clear`/`ace.reset` behavior for `*crdirty` and `*status.ACES` so implementers have a single, consistent requirement.
